_comment: Committed baseline for the search-relevance golden set. Regenerate deliberately and review the diff — never re-baseline to make a red build green. Metrics are measured over the frozen fixtures in ./fixtures and ./fixtures-web, so they only move when the ranker moves.
_lastMoveComment0: 2026-08-06, the LABELS were wrong, in both directions, and the ranker was not touched. P@5 0.973 -> 0.953 and MRR 0.974 -> 0.964; the category bucket falls 0.9 -> 0.75 and compound 0.992 -> 0.96, which is the whole move and is a ground-truth correction. The corpus had been scoring a hypernym query by whether a fruit word appeared anywhere in the name, so for 'Obst' it certified Hipp baby cereal, two Früchtequarks, three fruit bars and two smoothies as relevant while leaving Aprikosen, Datteln, Feigen, Nektarine, Pfirsich, Pflaumen, Physalis, Passionsfrucht and Pitahaya UNJUDGED — 15 labelled relevant, 8 of them not fruit, against 24 after relabelling. 'Gemüse' was worse: it scored a perfect P@5 on a top 5 holding a sweet-and-sour sauce, a vegan meat alternative and a vegetable juice, with Felix CAT FOOD ('Gemüse in Gel') also labelled relevant, and it forbade Gemüsebouillon while certifying Knorr Gemüse-Extrakt. Cause: German multi-word retail names lead with the product type and trail with the flavour ('Früchtequark Aprikose' is a quark), so a fruit lemma matches a slot that says nothing about what the thing is — while the existing head rule reads a single compound right-to-left, which is correct for 'Mischobst' and cannot help here. Fixed by naming the type explicitly in a new `related` list (ESCI Substitute/Complement) that outranks `relevant` but never gates, rather than by teaching this judge to parse title syntax — a corpus that exists to catch the ranker guessing must not contain a second guesser. 'Rüebli' was the same defect outside the category bucket, which is why compound moves too: Rüebli biscuits, a Rüebli cake, a carrot-orange-ginger juice and Betty Bossi marzipan carrots were all counted as the vegetable. Why it matters beyond the number: the old labels REWARDED ranking a baby purée at #1 for 'Obst' and would have scored a fix as a regression, which is why the band experiment recorded in the tracker could not be judged honestly. The corrected denominators also exposed two real filter defects that were invisible while the labels were wrong — 'Obst' drops Sultaninen, and 'Rüebli' keeps the biscuits while dropping nearly every actual carrot — both recorded in poolBaseline.json and left for the next matcher change rather than fixed in this diff.
_judgedAt5Comment: 2026-08-06, new metric: judged@5, the share of the scored top 5 carrying any label. P@5 counts an unlabelled product as non-relevant — the standard TREC pooling assumption — and that only holds while the labels cover what is retrieved, which nothing in P@5 announces. Ratcheted, never hard-gated on 'zero unjudged': the pools are recaptured from live vendors, so new products arrive on their own schedule and failing the build for that would make red mean 'the catalogue changed'. 0.996 today; the single unlabelled product is Coop's 'High Protein Apple-Cinnamon', left unjudged on purpose because its type is genuinely unstated in its identity (its category says Milchshake, which this judge deliberately cannot read). See Buckley & Voorhees, SIGIR '04.
_lastMoveComment: 2026-08-05, the judge was wrong and the number was never real. precisionAt5 0.98 -> 0.953 and mrr 0.987 -> 0.974 is a METRIC CORRECTION, not a ranking regression, and it is made of two separate moves measured separately. (1) judgeProduct matched a relevant label as a bare substring, so for 'Obst' it certified Obstessig (vinegar), Kernobstbranntwein (schnapps) and a Dr. Beckmann STAIN REMOVER as fruit and scored that query P@5 1.0. In a German compound the last stem says what the thing is, so a relevant label now has to land on the head; forbidden keeps matching anywhere, because Erdnussbutter is forbidden for 'Butter' precisely through its modifier. Ranker untouched, same fixtures: 0.98 -> 0.941. (2) the matcher fixes below then bought that back past where it started, to 0.973 on a fresh capture: category bucket 0.7 -> 0.9, romance 0.8 -> 0.9, multiword 0.92 -> 0.96, nothing fell. See _lastMoveComment2 for what the filter change was and how it was measured.
_lastMoveComment2: 2026-08-05, the mandatory-token rule was destroying recall and no metric could see it. Measured against pools captured BEFORE our own filter (fixtures-pool/, gated by poolRecall.test.ts): recall 0.768 -> 0.871 and, on the same frozen pools, P@5 0.941 -> 0.957 — precision ROSE, because for a category query the filter had been keeping only the junk that spelled the word out and dropping the actual products. Two causes, both morphology: TAXONOMY was keyed by English concept names ('fruit' -> ['obst',...]) and looked up by the shopper's German token, so 'obst' and 'teigwaren' expanded to nothing and, being unrecognised, became mandatory — 'Teigwaren' kept 10 of 87 relevant products, 'Reinigungsmittel' none of 32; and a closed compound ('Freilandeier') never matched the open form the retailer shelves it under ('Eier, Freiland').
_previousMoveComment: 2026-08-01, query understanding (modifier inflection + romance translation). coverage 0.902 -> 1.0: the 5 queries that returned nothing from any chain now return something. precisionAt5 0.991 -> 0.98 and mrr 1.0 -> 0.987 in the same change, and that is NOT a ranking regression — those two are means over *answered* queries only, so they were previously an average of the 46 easiest. End to end (every query counted, empty scored 0) went 0.894 -> 0.98 and 0.902 -> 0.987. Verified per query before re-baselining: no individual query's P@5 fell, 5 rose from 0. Only the 13 fixtures the change can affect were re-captured; the other 38 stay frozen so vendor drift is not in the same diff.
_tiersComment: vendor = raw 7-chain fan-out. web = the same fan-out plus web-search augmentation, which injects web-discovered products at the HEAD of the merged list and so can put a product in the top 5 that the vendor tier never saw. Both are gated; the local SQLite catalog is excluded from both because its contents are environment-specific and would make fixtures irreproducible.
_metricsComment: precisionAt5/mrr measure RANKING over queries that returned something. coverage is the answer rate and is gated separately: a query-understanding change that stops matching a hard class of queries would otherwise raise the ranking metrics by removing those queries from the average.
_knownGateViolationsComment: Empty on purpose in both tiers. The two defects this corpus was built around — Milchdrink UHT returning Milchschokolade, and Protein Milch returning bread — do NOT reproduce in either tier against the 2026-08-01 capture. They are not known to be fixed (matcher.ts last changed 2026-06-19, six weeks before they were reported), so the gate queries stay armed as regression guards rather than being recorded as accepted breakage.
_webTierComment: No web-tier fixtures are committed. Augmentation could not be captured honestly from this machine: the auto chain is ddg-html -> ddg-lite -> google-cse, and here both DDG endpoints return an HTTP 202 bot challenge while google CSE returns a permanent 400. The paid providers whose keys are configured are deliberately NOT in the auto chain (decided 2026-07-25 — DDG works through the deployed egress). A capture attempted anyway produced pools identical to the vendor tier for 49 of 51 queries, i.e. coverage in name only, so it was discarded rather than committed. Re-run `npm run eval:capture -- --web` from an egress DDG serves.
